title: Choosing a statistical test
caption: Match the test to the data and the question. Counts in categories compared with expected counts: chi-squared. An association between two measured variables: correlation. Comparing group means: a t-test for two normally distributed groups, ANOVA for three or more, and Mann–Whitney U for two groups that are not normally distributed.
alt: A flow chart from the kind of data and question to chi-squared, correlation, ANOVA, the Mann-Whitney U test or the t-test.
description: Are the data measurements rather than counts in categories? If not, compare the observed and expected counts with a chi-squared test.
Are you comparing groups? If not, you are testing for an association between two variables: correlation (Pearson or Spearman).
Are there exactly two groups? If not, compare three or more means with ANOVA.
Are the data normally distributed? If so, use a t-test; if not, the Mann–Whitney U test.

q1.q: Are the data measurements, not counts in categories?

chi.outcome: Chi-squared test: observed against expected frequencies

cor.outcome: Correlation (Pearson or Spearman): association of two variables

anova.outcome: ANOVA: means of three or more groups

mwu.outcome: Mann–Whitney U: two groups, no normality assumed
